5.1: The Hebrew says “your bone and your flesh”; BSB uses “your own flesh and blood.”
5.3: The Hebrew repeats “Hebron” and “David”; BSB omits the second place name and replaces the second personal name with “him.”
5.8: The Hebrew says “house”; BSB uses “palace.” It also explicitly names David where BSB uses “he.”
5.9: The Hebrew repeats “David”; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
5.12: The Hebrew says that his kingdom was exalted; BSB makes the LORD the explicit subject who exalted it.
5.13: The Hebrew repeats “David”; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “him.”
5.17: The Hebrew says that they anointed David, using an active verb; BSB says that David had been anointed.
5.19: The Hebrew says “Go up”; BSB says “Go.” The Hebrew also explicitly names David in the reply formula.
5.21: The Hebrew uses an unnamed plural subject; BSB identifies it as “the Philistines.”
5.23: The Hebrew says “Do not go up”; BSB adds “straight.” The Hebrew says to come to them, where BSB says to attack them.
5.25: The Hebrew names Geba; BSB names Gibeon.

6.2: The Hebrew says “from Baale-judah”; BSB says “for Baale of Judah.” It explicitly names David where BSB uses “he.”
6.4: The Hebrew repeats that they carried it from Abinadab’s house on the hill; this repetition is absent from BSB in this verse.
6.5: The Hebrew names cypress wood; BSB renders this as instruments of wood.
6.9: BSB adds “ever” to the question; the Hebrew asks how the ark of the LORD can come to David.
6.10: The Hebrew names David twice; BSB uses “he” in both places.
6.11: The Hebrew repeats “Obed-edom”; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “him.”
6.14: The Hebrew names David twice; BSB names him once.
6.15: The Hebrew explicitly names David; BSB uses “he.”
6.18: The Hebrew has a singular “burnt offering”; BSB uses the plural “burnt offerings.”
6.21: The Hebrew begins “Before the LORD”; BSB supplies “I was dancing” to complete the expression.
6.22: The Hebrew says “low in my own eyes”; BSB renders this as “humble myself.”
6.23: The Hebrew says “child” in the singular; BSB uses “children.”

7.2: The Hebrew explicitly says “the king,” where BSB uses “he.” It says “curtain,” where BSB uses “tent.”
7.6: The Hebrew says “in a tent and in a tabernacle”; BSB combines these as “with a tent as My dwelling.”
7.7: The Hebrew says “tribes of Israel”; BSB uses “leaders of Israel.”
7.9: The Hebrew says “a great name”; BSB says “a name.”
7.10: The Hebrew treats “My people Israel” as singular in the following pronouns and verbs; BSB uses plural forms.
7.11: The Hebrew repeats “the LORD”; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “He Himself.”
7.12: The Hebrew uses “seed” for the descendant and says “lie down” with the fathers; BSB uses “descendant” and “rest.”
7.15: The Hebrew says that His loving devotion will not depart; BSB expresses this passively as not being removed.
7.16: The Hebrew says “before you”; BSB says “before Me.”
7.17: The Hebrew distinguishes “all these words” and “all this vision”; BSB combines them as “all the words of this vision.”
7.19: The Hebrew uses the word “instruction” or “law” of man; BSB renders it as “custom with man.”
7.21: The Hebrew says “all this greatness” and describes making it known to the servant as a purpose; BSB says “this great thing” and states that it has been revealed.
7.27: The Hebrew uses the images of uncovering the servant’s ear and finding his heart; BSB uses “revealed” and “found the courage.”

8.2: The Hebrew calls Moab “servants”; BSB uses “subject.”
8.3: The Hebrew says “restore his hand”; BSB renders the image as restoring dominion.
8.4: The Hebrew has “a thousand and seven hundred horsemen”; BSB has “a thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers.”
8.6: The Hebrew says that the LORD saved David; BSB says that the LORD made David victorious.
8.7: The Hebrew calls Hadadezer’s men “servants”; BSB uses “officers.”
8.10: The Hebrew explicitly names Toi and says that the vessels were in his son’s hand; BSB uses “he” and says that the son brought them.
8.12: The Hebrew names Aram; BSB names Edom.
8.13: The Hebrew names Aram; BSB names the Edomites.
8.14: The Hebrew repeats the placing of garrisons and says that the LORD saved David; BSB mentions the placement once and says that the LORD made David victorious.
8.15: The Hebrew names David in both clauses; BSB combines the clauses under one occurrence of his name.
8.18: The Hebrew calls David’s sons “priests”; BSB uses “priestly leaders.”

13.1: The Hebrew first introduces Absalom’s beautiful sister and then says that Amnon loved her; BSB rearranges the clauses around Amnon.
13.4: The Hebrew addresses him as “son of the king”; BSB incorporates this into “you, the son of the king.”
13.5: The Hebrew explicitly mentions “bread”; BSB uses “something to eat.”
13.6: The Hebrew says “two cakes”; BSB says “a couple of cakes.”
13.9: The Hebrew says that she poured out the contents before him; BSB says that she set the pan down.
13.14: The Hebrew has an unnamed subject; BSB supplies “Amnon.”
13.15: The Hebrew repeats “Amnon” and the verbs for hating and loving; BSB replaces the second name with “he” and condenses the repeated verbs.
13.17: The Hebrew says “this one” without a noun; BSB supplies “woman.”
13.18: The Hebrew describes the garment before relating her removal; BSB puts her removal first and explicitly names Amnon and Tamar.
13.19: The Hebrew repeats the description of the distinctive tunic; BSB says only “her robe.” BSB also adds “bitterly.”
13.22: The Hebrew repeats Absalom’s name; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
13.23: The Hebrew repeats Absalom’s name; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
13.24: The Hebrew explicitly names Absalom and ends with “your servant”; BSB uses “he” and “me.” BSB also supplies “just hired.”
13.27: The Hebrew says that he sent Amnon and all the king’s sons “with him”; BSB leaves this phrase implicit.
13.29: The Hebrew says “all the king’s sons”; BSB adds “other.”
13.32: The Hebrew says “Let my lord not say”; BSB uses “must not think.”
13.34: The Hebrew says “behind him” and contains no speech reporting men from Horonaim; BSB says “west of him” and includes that report.
13.36: The Hebrew says that they lifted their voice and wept; BSB condenses this to “wailing loudly.”
13.37: The Hebrew leaves the mourner unnamed; BSB supplies “David.”

14.1: The Hebrew says the king’s heart was “toward Absalom”; BSB makes the longing explicit.
14.2: The Hebrew says that Joab took a woman from there; BSB presents bringing her as the purpose of his sending.
14.4: The Hebrew begins with the woman speaking to the king; BSB says that she went to him.
14.7: The Hebrew calls it “my ember that remains”; BSB adds “one.”
14.11: The Hebrew has an active plural clause, “they will not destroy my son”; BSB expresses it passively. BSB also supplies “head” in the promise about the hair.
14.13: The Hebrew says “his banished one”; BSB supplies “son.”
14.17: The Hebrew says “to hear the good and the evil”; BSB uses “discern good and evil.”
14.19: The Hebrew repeats the image of putting words into her mouth; BSB says that Joab told her exactly what to say.
14.20: The Hebrew says “turn the face of the matter”; BSB renders the image as bringing about a change of affairs.
14.21: The Hebrew says “I have done this thing”; BSB uses “I hereby grant this request.”
14.22: The Hebrew shifts from “your servant” to “I have found favor”; BSB maintains the third person.
14.24: The Hebrew says that he did not see “the king’s face”; BSB shortens this to seeing the king.
14.26: The Hebrew says “according to the king’s stone”; BSB renders the weight image as “according to the royal standard.”
14.29: The Hebrew explicitly names Absalom at the beginning; BSB uses “he.”
14.31: The Hebrew says that Joab arose and came; BSB omits his rising.
14.33: The Hebrew does not name David and repeats “the king”; BSB supplies “David” and replaces some repetitions with pronouns.

15.2: The Hebrew explicitly names Absalom in both opening and later clauses; BSB begins with “He.”
15.3: The Hebrew says that there is no one from the king to hear him; BSB supplies the office “deputy.”
15.4: The Hebrew explicitly names Absalom; BSB uses “he.”
15.5: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed; BSB supplies “Absalom.”
15.6: The Hebrew repeats Absalom’s name and uses singular “heart”; BSB uses “he” and plural “hearts.”
15.7: The Hebrew says “forty years”; BSB says “four years.”
15.9: The Hebrew leaves the departing subject unnamed; BSB supplies “Absalom.”
15.13: The Hebrew uses singular “heart” and collective singular “man of Israel”; BSB uses “hearts” and “men of Israel.”
15.14: The Hebrew says “the mouth of the sword”; BSB renders the image as putting the city to the sword.
15.16: The Hebrew repeats “the king” and says “house”; BSB uses “he” and “palace.”
15.19: The Hebrew says “the king”; BSB adds “new.”
15.20: The Hebrew ends with “loving devotion and faithfulness,” without an expressed subject or verb; BSB supplies “May the LORD show you.”
15.21: The Hebrew orders the alternatives as “death” and “life”; BSB reverses them.
15.24: The Hebrew says that Abiathar went up; BSB says that he offered sacrifices.
15.27: The Hebrew says “your two sons with you”; BSB makes explicit the pairing of each father and son.
15.28: The Hebrew says “plains of the wilderness”; BSB says “fords of the wilderness.”
15.30: The Hebrew says “ascent of the olives”; BSB calls it “the Mount of Olives.”
15.35: The Hebrew repeats the names and title “Zadok and Abiathar the priests” and says “house”; BSB uses “them” and “palace.”
15.36: The Hebrew says to send word “by their hand”; BSB says to send the sons with the information.
15.37: The Hebrew says Hushai came to “the city” and Absalom to “Jerusalem”; BSB reverses these designations.

16.3: The Hebrew says “son” and “father”; BSB interprets the relationships as “grandson” and “grandfather.”
16.6: The Hebrew repeats David’s name in “King David’s servants”; BSB omits it there and supplies it in the later phrase about his sides.
16.10: The Hebrew says “Thus let him curse”; BSB frames the clause as “If he curses me.”
16.11: The Hebrew says “who came out from my inward parts”; BSB renders this as “my own flesh and blood.”
16.12: The Hebrew repeats “the LORD”; BSB omits the second occurrence.
16.16: The Hebrew explicitly names Hushai in the speech formula and calls Absalom by name twice; BSB uses pronouns instead.
16.18: The Hebrew explicitly names Hushai and Absalom; BSB names only Hushai.
16.19: The Hebrew says “before his son” and “I will be before you”; BSB condenses the first and renders the second as serving.
16.20: The Hebrew command to give counsel is plural; BSB does not express this distinction.
16.21: The Hebrew explicitly names Ahithophel and Absalom and says “house”; BSB leaves the addressee implicit and uses “palace.”
16.22: The Hebrew repeats Absalom’s name; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
16.23: The Hebrew repeats “the counsel of Ahithophel”; BSB rearranges the second clause as the regard David and Absalom had for it.

21.1: The Hebrew says “in the days of David” and “the house of bloodshed”; BSB uses “during the reign of David” and speaks of blood shed by Saul and his family.
21.2: The Hebrew calls the speaker “the king”; BSB names David.
21.4: The Hebrew says that they have no man to put to death in Israel; BSB addresses David directly as the person who should not put anyone to death for them.
21.6: The Hebrew says “sons”; BSB uses “male descendants.”
21.8: The Hebrew names Michal; BSB names Merab.
21.10: The Hebrew says “water” poured from heaven “on them”; BSB specifies “rain” and “the bodies.”
21.12: The Hebrew explicitly names David and repeats “the Philistines”; BSB uses pronouns in those places.
21.13: The Hebrew has a separate active plural clause saying that they gathered the bones of those hanged; BSB combines those bones with the ones David had brought.
21.14: The Hebrew says that God was entreated for the land; BSB supplies the explicit phrase “answered their prayers.”
21.16: The Hebrew says that he was girded with a “new” item, leaving the noun implicit; BSB supplies “sword.”
21.17: The Hebrew addresses David as the one who might extinguish Israel’s lamp; BSB expresses the extinguishing passively.
21.19: The Hebrew names Jaare-oregim and says that Elhanan struck Goliath; BSB names Jair and supplies “the brother of Goliath.”
21.22: The Hebrew repeats “by the hand” for David and his servants; BSB combines them under one phrase.

22.1: The Hebrew says that David spoke the words of this song; BSB says that he sang it.
22.5: The Hebrew says that the torrents terrified him; BSB says that they overwhelmed him.
22.7: The Hebrew repeats the same verb for calling; BSB varies it as “called upon” and “cried out.” It ends “my cry in His ears,” where BSB supplies “reached.”
22.9: The Hebrew says that coals burned “from Him”; BSB leaves the source of the coals implicit.
22.10: The Hebrew says that He bent the heavens; BSB uses “parted.”
22.11: The Hebrew says that He was seen on the wings of the wind; BSB says that He soared.
22.12: The Hebrew uses plural “shelters”; BSB uses singular “a canopy.”
22.14: The Hebrew says that the Most High gave His voice; BSB makes “the voice” the subject that resounded.
22.15: The Hebrew does not explicitly name the targets as foes; BSB supplies “the foes.”
22.17: The Hebrew speaks of “many waters”; BSB says “deep waters.”
22.18: The Hebrew explicitly says “those who hate me” and “because they were stronger than I”; BSB condenses this to “foes too mighty for me.”
22.23: The Hebrew uses the image of not turning aside from His statutes; BSB says not disregarding them.
22.26: The Hebrew explicitly includes “man” in “a blameless mighty man”; BSB says “the blameless.”
22.30: The Hebrew says “leap over a wall”; BSB uses “scale a wall.”
22.31: The Hebrew calls the LORD’s word “refined”; BSB uses “flawless.”
22.34: The Hebrew says “my heights”; BSB says “the heights.”
22.37: The Hebrew says “my step”; BSB says “the path.”
22.40: The Hebrew says “girded me” with strength; BSB uses “armed me.”
22.41: The Hebrew says that He gave the enemies’ neck to David; BSB renders this image as making them retreat.
22.45: The Hebrew uses the image “sons of the foreigner” and “at the hearing of the ear”; BSB uses “foreigners” and “when they hear me.”
22.49: The Hebrew says “a man of violence” in the singular; BSB uses plural “violent men.”
22.51: The Hebrew uses “tower of salvations” and singular “seed”; BSB says “Great salvation He brings” and “descendants.”

23.4: The Hebrew explicitly repeats “morning”; BSB varies the second occurrence as “dawn.”
23.5: The Hebrew uses the image of making salvation and desire sprout; BSB renders it as bringing them about.
23.6: The Hebrew speaks of taking the thorns in the hand; BSB uses “gathered by hand.”
23.7: The Hebrew joins iron and the spear shaft with “and”; BSB uses “or.” It emphatically says that they will be burned, where BSB says that fire burns them to ashes.
23.8: The Hebrew includes the name Adino the Eznite; BSB instead says “He wielded his spear.”
23.9: The Hebrew says that the Philistines gathered “there”; BSB names Pas-dammim.
23.10: The Hebrew has an unnamed pronoun subject and says that his hand stuck to “the sword”; BSB names Eleazar and uses “his sword.” BSB also supplies “the dead” as the object of plundering.
23.12: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed; BSB supplies “Shammah.”
23.20: The Hebrew calls Benaiah the son of a valiant man; BSB calls Benaiah himself a man of valor.
23.21: The Hebrew repeatedly names “the Egyptian” but does not name Benaiah; BSB supplies Benaiah and replaces one occurrence of “the Egyptian” with a pronoun.
23.23: The Hebrew says he was honored above the Thirty; BSB says he was most honored among them.
23.24: The Hebrew places only Asahel explicitly “among the Thirty”; BSB supplies an introductory statement applying membership to the list.
23.29: The Hebrew names Heleb; BSB names Heled.
23.33: The Hebrew starts with Shammah the Hararite; BSB supplies “son of,” linking him to Jonathan in the preceding verse.
23.34: The Hebrew has another “son of” before “the Maacathite”; BSB omits that relationship word.

24.2: The Hebrew says “the people” twice; BSB uses “the troops” and then “their number.”
24.3: The Hebrew repeats the comparison “like them and like them”; BSB expresses only the hundredfold multiplication.
24.4: The Hebrew says “the people, Israel”; BSB uses “the troops of Israel.”
24.9: The Hebrew calls those counted “the people”; BSB calls them “the troops.”
24.10: The Hebrew says that David’s heart struck him and repeats David’s name; BSB uses “his conscience was stricken” and then “he.”
24.11: The Hebrew says “the word of the LORD”; BSB uses “a revelation from the LORD.”
24.13: The Hebrew says “seven years” of famine; BSB says “three years.”
24.17: The Hebrew repeats the speech formula and does not call David “the shepherd”; BSB combines the formulas and adds that title.
24.20: The Hebrew repeats Araunah’s name; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
24.23: The Hebrew repeats Araunah’s name; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
24.25: The Hebrew explicitly names David; BSB uses “he.” It says that the LORD was entreated for the land, where BSB supplies “answered the prayers.”
